title: What It Really Costs to Own a Bugatti Veyron

scenes.text: A new Bugatti Veyron cost about one point seven million dollars. A set of its tyres has been quoted at anything from twenty-five to forty-five thousand dollars. An oil change has been quoted at three thousand, twenty-one thousand, and thirty thousand dollars, by different people. And in twenty twenty-six one sold at auction for more than five million. This is what it really costs to own a Bugatti Veyron, and what the sources disagree about.
scenes.caption: WHAT IT REALLY COSTS TO OWN A BUGATTI VEYRON

scenes.text: We read Wikipedia, CNBC, Motor One, Motorious, Fox News, and the auction reports. The costs vary a lot between sources, so we show every figure with who said it. Where we do the arithmetic, it is labelled as ours. And where there is no published number, such as insurance, we say that plainly, because for the Veyron the missing numbers matter as much as the printed ones.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA · CNBC · MOTOR1 · MOTORIOUS · FOX NEWS · AUCTION REPORTS · OUR ARITHMETIC IS LABELLED

scenes.text: Start with the sticker. Wikipedia says the standard and Grand Sport base price was one million, two hundred twenty-five thousand euros, or about one point seven million dollars. The Super Sport and Grand Sport Vitesse started at one million, nine hundred twelve thousand, five hundred euros, or about two point seven million dollars. A tuned Mansory Linea Vivere cost two point three million dollars.
scenes.caption: €1,225,000 (~$1.7M) STANDARD/GRAND SPORT · €1,912,500 (~$2.7M) SUPER SPORT/VITESSE · MANSORY LINEA VIVERE $2.3M (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Put those in context using the Census Bureau's median household income for twenty twenty-four, eighty-three thousand, seven hundred thirty dollars. By our arithmetic, the one point seven million dollar base price is twenty point three years of median household income, and the two point seven million dollar Super Sport is thirty-two point two years. These are gross incomes before tax.
scenes.caption: $1.7M ≈ 20.3 YEARS · $2.7M ≈ 32.2 YEARS OF MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME ($83,730, CENSUS) (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Against the average new vehicle, fifty thousand, eighty-nine dollars in August twenty twenty-six according to Kelley Blue Book, the base Veyron is about thirty-four times as much, by our arithmetic. The Super Sport's price is about fifty-four. And compared with the Ford Mustang GTD at three hundred twenty-seven thousand, nine hundred sixty dollars, the base Veyron price is about five times.
scenes.caption: $1.7M ≈ 33.9× AVERAGE NEW VEHICLE ($50,089, KBB) · $2.7M ≈ 53.9× · ≈ 5.2× MUSTANG GTD ($327,960, MOTOR1) (OUR ARITHMETIC)
scenes.orig_query: Veyron price vs average new vehicle

scenes.text: Jeremy Clarkson, quoted by Wikipedia, said the production cost was five million pounds and customers paid one million. Motor One says Volkswagen reportedly lost about six point two five million dollars on each of the four hundred fifty it sold. Jalopnik traces that figure to an Economist infographic from September twenty thirteen, and says it does not explain the method. So the buyer got a car that cost far more to make than they paid.
scenes.caption: CLARKSON: £5M COST vs £1M PRICE (WIKIPEDIA) · ~$6.25M LOSS PER CAR (MOTOR1; JALOPNIK CITING THE ECONOMIST, METHOD NOT EXPLAINED)

scenes.text: That gap matters for ownership in an unexpected way. If the manufacturer lost money on every car, its service pricing is not the same as a profit-making brand's. We have no source linking the two, so this is not a claim. It is a question: when a maker lost millions per car, is the cost of parts and labour a reflection of the real cost? Our sources do not answer it.
scenes.caption: WAS SERVICE PRICING SHAPED BY THE LOSSES? — NO SOURCE LINKS THE TWO

scenes.text: Tyres first, because they are the most quoted cost. Wikipedia says the Michelin PAX run-flat tyres cost twenty-five thousand dollars per set, and that mounting them on the wheels was only available in France, at seventy thousand dollars. Car magazine adds that the PAX tyres are designed to last about fifteen minutes at top speed. So the set that costs twenty-five thousand has a defined limit.
scenes.caption: PAX TYRES $25,000 PER SET · MOUNTING (FRANCE ONLY) $70,000 (WIKIPEDIA) · DESIGNED FOR ~15 MINUTES AT TOP SPEED (CAR MAGAZINE)

scenes.text: CNBC, in September twenty eighteen, quotes Bugatti dealer staff saying tyres alone are currently around thirty-eight thousand dollars. Motor One says a set of Veyron tyres can cost thirty thousand. And Motorious, in April twenty twenty-six, reports a YouTuber owner saying roughly forty-five thousand dollars for a full set. So four sources give four different figures for the same item.
scenes.caption: $25,000 (WIKIPEDIA) · $30,000 (MOTOR1) · $38,000 (CNBC, 2018, CROSTA) · ~$45,000 (MOTORIOUS, APRIL 2026, OWNER'S ACCOUNT)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the highest figure is eighty percent above the lowest: forty-five over twenty-five. The sources are from different years, and prices change, so the spread may reflect time, not disagreement. But even the lowest figure is more than the price of an average new vehicle at fifty thousand, eighty-nine dollars, in half. A set of tyres costs half a new car.
scenes.caption: $45,000 ÷ $25,000 = 1.8 (+80%) · $25,000 ≈ 49.9% OF THE AVERAGE NEW VEHICLE ($50,089) (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Add the mounting. Wikipedia's seventy thousand dollar figure for mounting in France, on top of twenty-five thousand for the tyres, is ninety-five thousand dollars, by our arithmetic. Kelley Blue Book's table lists the Corvette ZR1 at one hundred seventy-eight thousand, one hundred ninety-five dollars, so one tyre change on a Veyron, on those figures, is about fifty-three percent of a ZR1's price.
scenes.caption: $25,000 + $70,000 = $95,000 ≈ 53% OF A ZR1's $178,195 TABLE PRICE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The wheels and the tyres are not the only parts that wear. Wikipedia says parts shared with other Volkswagen Group models can wear quickly under the car's heavy loads, though this makes independent repairs easier. So there are two kinds of parts on a Veyron: those unique to it, which are very expensive, and those shared with Volkswagen cars, which wear out faster than they would in a normal car.
scenes.caption: SHARED VW GROUP PARTS CAN WEAR QUICKLY UNDER HEAVY LOADS — BUT INDEPENDENT REPAIRS EASIER (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: The oil change is the legend. Motor One tells of a twenty oh eight Veyron brought to Apple Autos in Minnesota, where Austin Paseka, a video and media specialist, quoted the oil change at probably around thirty thousand dollars, for about twenty-seven hours of labour. The article says the Veyron has sixteen drain plugs, and that the job requires removing underbody panels, the rear fender and the deck lid.
scenes.caption: 2008 VEYRON AT APPLE AUTOS, MINNESOTA: 'PROBABLY AROUND $30,000' · ~27 HOURS · 16 DRAIN PLUGS (AUSTIN PASEKA, MOTOR1)

scenes.text: Motor One adds that Carscoops has reported an average Veyron oil change of twenty-one to twenty-five thousand dollars, and puts it at about two thousand dollars per drain plug. By our arithmetic, sixteen plugs at two thousand is thirty-two thousand, so the per-plug figure and the thirty thousand estimate are in the same range. Only certified centres can do the work, and the process can take up to a week.
scenes.caption: CARSCOOPS (VIA MOTOR1): $21,000–$25,000 · ~$2,000 PER PLUG × 16 = $32,000 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · CERTIFIED CENTRES ONLY · UP TO A WEEK (MOTOR1)

scenes.text: For comparison, Motor One lists a Lamborghini Huracán oil change at about twelve hundred dollars, a Ferrari four eighty-eight at about fifteen hundred, and a McLaren seven twenty S at more than two thousand at some dealerships. By our arithmetic, a twenty-one thousand dollar Veyron oil change is seventeen and a half times a Huracán's, and a thirty thousand dollar one is twenty-five times.
scenes.caption: HURACÁN ~$1,200 · 488 ~$1,500 · 720S >$2,000 (MOTOR1) · VEYRON $21,000 ≈ 17.5× HURACÁN · $30,000 = 25× (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: And now the disagreement. Motorious, in April twenty twenty-six, reports a YouTuber who owns a Veyron Grand Sport saying an oil change runs between three thousand and four thousand dollars. By our arithmetic, that is one tenth to one fifth of the Carscoops range. The article does not say why. It could be a different shop, a different year, or a different scope of work, but our sources do not tell us.
scenes.caption: OWNER'S ACCOUNT (MOTORIOUS, APRIL 2026): $3,000–$4,000 vs $21,000–$30,000 ELSEWHERE · REASON NOT STATED

scenes.text: The same owner says an annual service approaches twenty thousand dollars, Motorious reports. CNBC, in twenty eighteen, quotes Bugatti dealer staff saying the oil is changed once a year, whether the car has been driven or not, as part of a service that covers all fluids. By our arithmetic, twenty thousand a year is about one point two percent of a one point seven million dollar price every year.
scenes.caption: ANNUAL SERVICE 'APPROACHES $20,000' (MOTORIOUS) · ONCE A YEAR, DRIVEN OR NOT (CNBC 2018) · $20,000 ÷ $1.7M ≈ 1.2% PER YEAR (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Parts of the maintenance are not about money alone. Motor One says Bugatti's maintenance guide calls for inspecting hydraulic lines, gaskets and proprietary fluids, and that only certified centres can do the work. CNBC says the service is meant to keep the car running at its highest output and efficiency. So an owner cannot simply take a Veyron to any garage, which limits the choices on price.
scenes.caption: INSPECTIONS OF HYDRAULIC LINES, GASKETS, PROPRIETARY FLUIDS · CERTIFIED CENTRES ONLY (MOTOR1) · SERVICE KEEPS 'HIGHEST OUTPUT AND EFFICIENCY' (CNBC)

scenes.text: Bigger parts cost more. Wikipedia says a replacement transmission costs just over one hundred twenty thousand dollars. By our arithmetic, that is seven percent of the base price, and about two and a half times the highest tyre quote. The page does not say how often a transmission needs replacing, so we cannot turn it into an annual cost.
scenes.caption: REPLACEMENT TRANSMISSION JUST OVER $120,000 ≈ 7.1% OF $1.7M (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC) · REPLACEMENT INTERVAL: NOT STATED

scenes.text: Fuel. Wikipedia gives the Veyron's EPA fuel economy as eight miles per gallon in the city and fourteen on the highway, and three miles per gallon at top speed, which is one point four gallons a minute. By our arithmetic, ten thousand miles at eight miles per gallon would burn twelve hundred fifty gallons, and at fourteen about seven hundred fourteen. Multiply by the price of fuel where you live.
scenes.caption: EPA: 8 CITY · 14 HIGHWAY · 3 MPG AT TOP SPEED (1.4 GAL/MIN) · 10,000 MI → 1,250 GAL (CITY) · ~714 GAL (HIGHWAY) (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: At top speed, the tank is a short-lived resource. Car magazine says the car drains its hundred litre tank in twelve minutes at full speed. By our arithmetic, that is about eight and a third litres a minute, or two point two gallons, which is higher than Wikipedia's one point four. The two sources disagree, and we cannot tell which is right, but neither suggests top speed is a cheap place to be.
scenes.caption: CAR MAGAZINE: 100 L IN 12 MIN ≈ 2.2 GAL/MIN vs WIKIPEDIA 1.4 GAL/MIN — DISAGREE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Insurance. We found no published Veyron insurance figure in the sources we read. Storage, battery maintenance, registration, and the cost of an annual inspection also appear in none of them. So a large part of the ownership bill is simply not documented in our sources. If you know of a reliable published figure, share the link in the comments, and we will add it.
scenes.caption: INSURANCE · STORAGE · REGISTRATION · BATTERY: NO PUBLISHED FIGURES IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: One more cost, the rental. CNBC reports that Royalty Exotic Cars rents a Bugatti Veyron for twenty thousand dollars including taxes for twenty-four hours, and that the company does not rent Bugattis for recreational driving, but for film productions, photo shoots, trade shows and conventions. By our arithmetic, a day's rental is about one point two percent of the original price of one point seven million.
scenes.caption: RENTAL $20,000 PER 24 HOURS INCL. TAXES (ROYALTY EXOTIC CARS, CNBC 2018) · ≈ 1.2% OF $1.7M (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Now resale, where the story is surprising. Motorious reports that a twenty ten Bugatti Veyron coupe sold for two million, two hundred five thousand dollars at Broad Arrow Auctions' inaugural Las Vegas auction on the thirty-first of October, twenty twenty-five, including the buyer's premium, against a pre-sale estimate of one point five to one point eight million. The article calls it a world record for a standard Veyron at auction.
scenes.caption: 2010 VEYRON COUPE: $2,205,000 INCL. PREMIUM · EST. $1.5M–$1.8M · BROAD ARROW, LAS VEGAS, OCT 31, 2025 · 'WORLD RECORD FOR A STANDARD VEYRON AT AUCTION' (MOTORIOUS)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the price was twenty-two and a half percent above the high end of the estimate, and about thirty percent above the base price of one point seven million dollars that Wikipedia quotes for a new car. The price is a sale result including fees, and the car was a twenty ten model, so the comparison with a base price is rough, but a used Veyron selling above its new price is notable.
scenes.caption: $2,205,000 vs $1.8M HIGH ESTIMATE = +22.5% · vs $1.7M BASE = +29.7% (OUR ARITHMETIC; DIFFERENT YEARS)

scenes.text: Motorious quotes Broad Arrow's Alexander Weaver: we saw tremendous demand for original, unmodified Veyrons, this result reinforced that momentum. The auction's total sales were thirteen million, seven hundred sixteen thousand, eight hundred forty dollars, with eighty-two percent of lots sold. By our arithmetic, the Veyron was sixteen percent of the whole auction's sales.
scenes.caption: WEAVER: 'TREMENDOUS DEMAND FOR ORIGINAL, UNMODIFIED VEYRONS' · AUCTION TOTAL $13,716,840 · 82% SOLD · VEYRON ≈ 16.1% OF TOTAL (MOTORIOUS; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: A year later came a bigger number. A report dated the thirtieth of September, twenty twenty-six, says a twenty fourteen Veyron Grand Sport Vitesse called Jean-Pierre Wimille, chassis ending seven nine five zero six three, hammered at RM Sotheby's for four million, five hundred five thousand Swiss francs, about five point four million dollars, against an estimate of 2.4 to 2.8 million francs. It had 3,766 kilometres on it.
scenes.caption: 2014 GRAND SPORT VITESSE 'JEAN-PIERRE WIMILLE': CHF 4,505,000 (~$5.4M) · EST. CHF 2.4–2.8M · 3,766 KM · RM SOTHEBY'S, SEPT 2026 (AUTOEVOLUTION)

scenes.text: The report says the hammer was sixty-one percent above the high estimate, and by our arithmetic four million five hundred five thousand over two point eight million is indeed sixty-one percent above. It calls the car the most expensive Veyron ever sold at public auction, beating the one-off Grand Sport Sang Bleu, which sold for a little over three million dollars in twenty twenty-four. Bidding lasted under three minutes.
scenes.caption: HAMMER = +60.9% ABOVE HIGH ESTIMATE (OUR ARITHMETIC) · BEAT THE ONE-OFF SANG BLEU (~$3M+, 2024) · BIDDING UNDER 3 MINUTES (AUTOEVOLUTION)

scenes.text: It was a special car: the opening of a series of six Grand Sport Vitesse editions, three units each, each honouring a pre-war Bugatti racing figure, and it was delivered new to a Dubai-based client. By our arithmetic, the five point four million dollar result is about twice the two point seven million dollar Grand Sport Vitesse list price in Wikipedia. A special edition with low mileage is not a typical Veyron.
scenes.caption: ONE OF SIX EDITIONS, 3 UNITS EACH · FIRST OWNER IN DUBAI · $5.4M ≈ 2.0× THE $2.7M LIST PRICE (AUTOEVOLUTION, WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The other end of the market. Fox News reported in August twenty fourteen that a crashed twenty oh eight Veyron with thirty-one thousand, nine hundred twenty-four kilometres sold in Switzerland for two hundred fifty-four thousand francs, about two hundred seventy-seven thousand dollars, after a single-vehicle accident on an Austrian highway. The seller estimated repairs at eight hundred to eight hundred fifty-five thousand dollars.
scenes.caption: 2008 VEYRON, 31,924 KM, CRASHED IN AUSTRIA: SOLD CHF 254,000 (~$277,344) · REPAIR ESTIMATE $800,000–$855,000 (FOX NEWS, AUG 2014)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the repair estimate was between 2.9 and 3.1 times the sale price. Fox calls the sale the deal of a century, and wonders who would bid. The car had damage to the front, rear, doors, sills, underbody and suspension, with engine and transmission at risk. That is the price of a crash: a Veyron's repair bill can be a multiple of what a wrecked one sells for.
scenes.caption: $800,000 ÷ $277,344 = 2.9× · $855,000 ÷ $277,344 = 3.1× (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Convert the tyre and service bills into the yardstick we used earlier. A tyre change with mounting in France, ninety-five thousand dollars on Wikipedia's figures, is one point one three years of median household income, by our arithmetic. A thirty thousand dollar oil change is about four months of that income, and a twenty-one thousand dollar one about three months. These are gross figures, before tax.
scenes.caption: $95,000 ÷ $83,730 ≈ 1.13 YEARS · $30,000 ≈ 4.3 MONTHS · $21,000 ≈ 3.0 MONTHS OF MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: An illustration, clearly labelled as ours and not a forecast. Take a year with one oil change and one set of tyres. The lowest figures in our sources are three thousand for the oil and twenty-five thousand for the tyres, twenty-eight thousand in total. The highest are thirty thousand and forty-five thousand, seventy-five thousand. By our arithmetic, that is between one point six and four point four percent of the one point seven million dollar price.
scenes.caption: ILLUSTRATION, NOT A FORECAST: $3K + $25K = $28K (1.6% OF $1.7M) TO $30K + $45K = $75K (4.4%) (OUR ARITHMETIC FROM THE RANGE OF QUOTES)

scenes.text: Why not a real annual total? Because our sources do not say how often tyres are changed, how many miles an owner drives, or what the insurance and storage cost. A car driven rarely could go years on one set of tyres, though a tyre of that age may not be safe, and we have no source on tyre age limits. So any annual figure we gave would be a guess, and we do not guess.
scenes.caption: TYRE CHANGE INTERVAL · MILEAGE · INSURANCE · STORAGE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES → NO ANNUAL TOTAL GIVEN

scenes.text: The top-speed tyre arithmetic is amusing but useful. If a set is designed for about fifteen minutes at top speed, as Car magazine says, and covers sixty-three and a half miles at two hundred fifty-four miles per hour, then a twenty-five thousand dollar set works out at about three hundred ninety-four dollars per mile at that speed, by our arithmetic, and a forty-five thousand dollar set at about seven hundred nine.
scenes.caption: $25,000 ÷ 63.5 MI ≈ $394/MILE · $45,000 ÷ 63.5 MI ≈ $709/MILE AT TOP SPEED (OUR ARITHMETIC; ILLUSTRATION ONLY)

scenes.text: And the fuel in the same fifteen minutes. At one point four gallons a minute, Wikipedia's figure, that is twenty-one gallons, by our arithmetic. At Car magazine's rate of about two point two gallons a minute, it would be about thirty-three. Either way, a fifteen-minute run at top speed burns twenty to thirty gallons and uses up a set of tyres worth tens of thousands of dollars.
scenes.caption: 15 MIN × 1.4 GAL/MIN = 21 GAL · 15 MIN × 2.2 GAL/MIN ≈ 33 GAL (OUR ARITHMETIC FROM WIKIPEDIA AND CAR MAGAZINE)

scenes.text: Back to the thirty thousand dollar oil change, for twenty-seven hours of labour. By our arithmetic, that is about eleven hundred dollars per hour, but that is an all-in figure that includes oil, filters and everything else, not a labour rate. We have no breakdown. And twenty-seven hours is a week of work in a shop with other cars waiting, which explains why Motor One says the job can take up to a week.
scenes.caption: $30,000 ÷ 27 H ≈ $1,111/H ALL-IN (NOT A LABOUR RATE; OUR ARITHMETIC) · UP TO A WEEK (MOTOR1)

scenes.text: Rental gives a different view of cost. At twenty thousand dollars a day, CNBC's figure for Royalty Exotic Cars, the original one point seven million dollar price equals eighty-five days of rental, by our arithmetic. The company says the rentals are for films, photo shoots and trade shows, not recreational driving.
scenes.caption: $1.7M ÷ $20,000 = 85 DAYS OF RENTAL (OUR ARITHMETIC) · RENTALS FOR FILMS, PHOTO SHOOTS, TRADE SHOWS (ROYALTY EXOTIC CARS, CNBC 2018)

scenes.text: Price over time, in the sources. New, about one point seven million dollars. Wrecked in twenty fourteen, two hundred seventy-seven thousand. A twenty ten coupe in October twenty twenty-five, two point two oh five million. A twenty fourteen special edition in September twenty twenty-six, about five point four million. The one-off Sang Bleu a little over three million in twenty twenty-four. These are different cars, so it is not a trend line.
scenes.caption: NEW ~$1.7M · WRECK 2014 $277K · 2010 COUPE OCT 2025 $2.205M · SANG BLEU 2024 ~$3M+ · WIMILLE SEPT 2026 ~$5.4M — DIFFERENT CARS, NOT A TREND

scenes.text: There is one more cost we should not forget, the cost of being wrong about a number. The oil change figures vary tenfold, the tyre figures by eighty percent, the fuel figures by more than fifty. Anyone budgeting for a Veyron on one article would be misled. The responsible approach is to get written quotes from certified Bugatti service centres, and the sources suggest that is the only route anyway.
scenes.caption: OIL $3K–$30K (10×) · TYRES $25K–$45K (+80%) · FUEL RATE 1.4–2.2 GAL/MIN (+57%) · CERTIFIED CENTRES ONLY (MOTOR1)

scenes.text: Finally, the Chiron. Wikipedia says its base price was two point four million euros, and Bugatti's press release says the Chiron Super Sport has a WLTP combined consumption of twenty-one point five litres per hundred kilometres. Our sources do not give Chiron service or tyre costs. So the Veyron, for all its reputation, is simply the better documented of the two when it comes to what it costs to keep.
scenes.caption: CHIRON BASE €2.4M (WIKIPEDIA) · SUPER SPORT 21.5 L/100 KM (BUGATTI) · CHIRON SERVICE/TYRE COSTS: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: So what does it really cost to own a Bugatti Veyron? On the figures we can show: one point seven million dollars new for the base car, twenty-five to forty-five thousand for a set of tyres depending on who you ask, an annual service approaching twenty thousand, an oil change quoted anywhere between three thousand and thirty thousand, a transmission above one hundred twenty thousand, and fuel at eight to fourteen miles per gallon.
scenes.caption: NEW $1.7M · TYRES $25K–$45K · ANNUAL SERVICE ~$20K · OIL CHANGE $3K–$30K · TRANSMISSION >$120K · 8–14 MPG

scenes.text: Our reference price for this video is one point seven million dollars, the base price of the standard Veyron in Wikipedia. It is a published new-car figure. The used market has since gone far above it for good cars, and far below it for wrecks. And between the two sits a service bill that no two sources describe the same way, which is the main lesson of this video.
scenes.caption: REFERENCE PRICE: $1.7 MILLION (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: What our sources do not say. Insurance. Storage. Registration. How often tyres, transmissions or other big parts need replacing. Whether the oil change quotes differ by year, shop or scope. And what a typical Veyron costs to run in a year. If you have a reliable published source for any of them, share it in the comments, and we will update the description.
scenes.caption: NOT PUBLISHED: INSURANCE · STORAGE · REGISTRATION · PART REPLACEMENT INTERVALS · WHY OIL CHANGE QUOTES DIFFER · TYPICAL ANNUAL RUNNING COST

scenes.text: Would you take a Veyron at today's auction prices, knowing what the service might cost? Tell us in the comments. In the other videos of this series, we reveal two things you did not know about the Veyron, compare it with the Chiron, and tell why it almost never happened. Our twenty twenty-seven Truck Buyer's Guide is linked in the description. Subscribe to Pickup Reality.
scenes.caption: SUBSCRIBE: PICKUP REALITY
